authority: User comments and original proposal; minimal factual corrections approved 2026-11-07

points.title: World building
points.caption: For fantasy and sci-fi movies, AI could quickly generate backdrops and action instead of requiring some real sets and props. [1]

points.title: Consistent style & props
points.caption: It is hard to keep props and style consistent throughout a movie. With AI videos, referencing images can help, though results still need checking. [1,3]

points.title: Low cost for redos
points.caption: AI-generated shots can be cheaper and easier to regenerate than traditional reshoots, which may require rebuilding sets and recalling crews. [1]

points.title: Teaching & demonstrations
points.caption: Supports teaching and topic demonstrations (e.g., Google NotebookLM), which could produce teaching videos and slide decks. [26]

points.title: Creative ideas
points.caption: Lets people imagine themselves or their IPs in different situations, making prompts a strong source of creative ideas. [1]

points.title: Low variety
points.caption: The base model could produce very similar scenes or characters. Copying others’ work or using someone’s likeness without permission can raise rights concerns. [5,20]

points.title: Deepfake abuse
points.caption: Shorts could feature real people in undesirable or sexual settings, harming their reputations. Videos of loved ones may be used to threaten or scam family members. [19,23]

points.title: Labour & consent
points.caption: AI could affect traditional film workers’ jobs, wages and creative control. Reusing someone’s appearance or voice raises consent and credit concerns. [6,20]

points.title: Reality or fiction?
points.caption: As AI videos become more realistic, people may become confused about what is real and more vulnerable to fake news. [21]

points.title: Revenue limits
points.caption: YouTube may reject repetitively produced AI junk, while people making similar videos may also face monetisation restrictions. [10]

necessaryCorrections: Replaced unsupported tens-of-dollars versus millions comparison with lower reshoot costs.
Reference images help consistency; they do not guarantee it.
Similarity alone does not establish rights infringement.
Replaced unsupported judgement-degradation claim with misleading viewers about reality.
Distinguished 2023 strikes from the 2026 Seedance dispute.
